authors.name: Xiaoli Li
affiliation: Information Systems Technology and Design Pillar, Singapore University of Technology and Design, Tampines, Singapore

p: Xiaoli Li (Fellow, IEEE) is currently a Full Professor and the Head of Pillar with the Information Systems Technology and Design (ISTD) Pillar, Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), Singapore. He also holds an appointment as an Adjunct Full Professor with Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. He has published more than 390 papers in leading journals and conferences, with research interests including artificial intelligence (AI), data mining, machine learning, and bioinformatics.

Dr. Li is a fellow of AAIA. He has served as the area chair or senior program committee member for several premier AI and data mining conferences, and has received ten Best Paper and Benchmark Competition Awards. He is the Editor-in-Chief of the World Scientific Annual Review of Artificial Intelligence and serves as an Associate Editor of IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence, Knowledge and Information Systems, and Machine Learning With Applications (Elsevier). Beyond academia, he actively collaborates with the industry, having established and led multiple joint laboratories and spearheaded more than ten major research and development partnerships with global organizations in aerospace, telecommunications, insurance, and professional services. His work has been internationally recognized, including being listed among the world’s top 2% of scientists in AI (Stanford University) and as a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher.

data.formulaStrippedArticleTitle: Brain Cognition-Inspired Adaptable LLM Agents for Continuous Knowledge Reuse Across Tasks in IoT
data.authorNames: Tao Chen;MengMeng Sui;Baoyu Zhang;Shaohua Cao;Weishan Zhang;Lianyong Qi;Xiaoli Li
data.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are promising in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. However, existing agent systems suffer from an ephemeral limitation: agents are instantiated for individual tasks and terminated upon completion, losing valuable execution experiences across different tasks where past knowledge reuse is impossible. Inspired by dual-process theory in cognitive science, we propose a brain cognition-inspired dual-system agent framework for continuous knowledge reuse across heterogeneous task streams, termed the cognition-inspired dual-system agent framework for continuous knowledge reuse (CIA-CKR). The CIA-CKR framework separates fast (reactive execution) from slow (deliberative planning) cognition phases by maintaining a persistent knowledge base throughout the operational lifetime of agents. Two synergistic mechanisms are designed that mirror bidirectional knowledge flow in human cognition: a personalized agent generation mechanism that retrieves task-relevant knowledge and configures context-specific agent capabilities through top-down adaptation, and a knowledge accumulation mechanism that extracts experiential insights from execution traces through bottom-up feedback. Extensive experiments on HomeBench (smart home control) and OmniEAR (embodied multiagent collaboration) datasets demonstrate that CIA-CKR consistently outperforms both vanilla LLMs and recent memory-augmented methods, achieving 10.82% and 4.23% average accuracy improvements on HomeBench and OmniEAR, respectively, over the best baselines.
